title: Israel launches ground operation in central Gaza; Jeffries wins speaker nomination; NSA’s internal comms system goes down
author: Drop Site News
content:
**Wednesday, November 18, 2026 - **

_**Iran:** U.S. strikes Iran's Qeshm Island; Iran widens Gulf attacks to
Kuwait. UAE oil vessel attacked in Hormuz, one crew member missing and 11
injured. Iran says U.S. "dirty bomb" claims echo Iraq war propaganda; Rubio
says no imminent threat. U.S. Navy says Iran war is straining resources,
requiring use of previously expired munitions. Iran says it downed U.S. drone
near Hormuz. AI models repeatedly identify civilians, Iranian school as
military targets, study finds._

_**Palestine:** Israeli attacks kill three Palestinians across Gaza. Israeli
forces launch first large-scale military operation in central Gaza since
"ceasefire." Israel restricts medical evacuations, Gaza Health Ministry says;
over 21,000 patients await treatment abroad. Israeli forces detain 26
Palestinians across occupied West Bank. Israel orders land seizure in Tulkarm
and Nur Shams refugee camps. Israel extends detention of Gaza hospital
director Hussam Abu Safiya another six months without charge. U.S.-backed
Board of Peace says Gaza ceasefire risks collapse. Australia sanctions Israeli
settler leader Daniella Weiss and construction firm over West Bank
settlements. Hind Rajab Foundation seeks U.S. prosecution of former Israeli
defense minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and genocide._

_**Yemen:** Saudi airstrikes kill 15 at factory in Hodeidah, Yemen. Saudi-led
coalition says it destroyed 60 Ansarallah targets across Yemen, intercepted
missile near Riyadh._

_**U.S.:** Hakeem Jeffries wins speaker nomination, commits to aggressive
agenda on immigration, healthcare ahead of vote. NSA reports outage of
classified comms system. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin defends use of
government plane to attend college football game. Kalshi halts bets predicting
Trump statements. Politico: Hegseth's personal attorney represents son of
Libyan warlord. Pentagon fails annual audit for ninth consecutive year.
Federal appeals court stops Pentagon's attempt to expel 27 transgender troops
from military. Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years in prison for attempt to
assassinate U.S. politician; he says Iran backed the plot. Mary Peltola wins
Senate race in Alaska, bringing Dem majority to 56 seats. NYT: IRS pursuing
criminal investigations of left-wing groups. White House abandons FDA nominee.
DOJ misconduct complaints rise 54% under second Trump administration.
Massachusetts town passes BDS measure._

_**International:** Brazilian federal police investigating Vance donor network
for election interference. Pentagon policy secretary tells Europeans not to
exclude American weapons firms from deals ahead of troop review. Boat strike
survivors sue Trump administration. U.S. soldier arrested in Britain on
suspicion of spying for Russia is transferred to U.S. military custody.
Mexico's Sheinbaum tells China's Xi she wants deeper economic cooperation.
Peru's Fujimori seeks China's help on El Niño, says Beijing pledged $22.5
million in aid. Clashes between police and garment workers in Bangladesh
escalate. Over 146,000 take to French streets as public-sector workers demand
pay raises amid rising cost of living. Mozambique opposition leader goes on
trial. Trump announces critical-minerals agreements with Quad partners India,
Australia and Japan at Manila meeting._

**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *

# Iran

  * **U.S. strikes Iran 's Qeshm Island; Iran widens Gulf attacks to Kuwait:** U.S. fighter jets [carried out](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-strikes-iranian-missile-launch-site-qeshm-island-us-official-says-2026-11-17/) airstrikes on a missile-launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tuesday, a U.S. military official told Reuters. The official said that the attack followed Iranian strikes on American personnel and assets.

    * Early Wednesday, the Iranian military [said](https://en.irna.ir/news/86325322/Iranian-Army-targets-US-Patriot-systems-at-Kuwait-s-Ali-Al-Salem) that it launched drones targeting U.S. Patriot air defense systems and missile and drone launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait. It is the first Iranian attack on the country in more than two months. Kuwait's military reported a wave of incoming drones.

    * In Bahrain, missile alerts sounded twice before dawn on Wednesday as air defenses fired and explosions were heard, with authorities blaming Iran for the attack. Iran has claimed responsibility for three attacks on U.S. assets in Bahrain over the past week.

    * Iranian Army Chief Amir Hatami [warned](https://en.irna.ir/news/86325626/Iran-s-Army-chief-warns-of-stronger-response-to-any-renewed-aggression) that further U.S. attacks on Iran would be met with a more forceful response "without geographical restrictions."

  * **UAE oil vessel attacked in Hormuz, one crew member missing and 11 injured:** A vessel of Abu Dhabi National Oil Company's shipping arm, ADNOC Logistics & Services, was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday evening, the Emirati state-owned company [confirmed](https://adnocls.ae/en/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/november-17-statement). One crew member remains missing, while 11 others were injured. All other crew members were safely evacuated, the company said.

    * Three vessels struck naval mines in Hormuz on Tuesday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said, including a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil and a liquefied petroleum gas carrier.

  * **Iran says U.S. "dirty bomb" claims echo Iraq war propaganda; Rubio says no imminent threat: **U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio [said](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/tehran-denies-report-potential-iranian-plan-detonate-dirty-bomb-washington-2026-11-17/) on Wednesday that he does not believe there is an imminent threat to Washington, D.C. His comment follows a CNN report, citing U.S. intelligence assessments, that suggested that Iran may be planning to target senior Trump administration officials with a "dirty bomb" or a chemical weapon. "I don't think there is any imminent threat," Rubio told reporters.

    * Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [called](https://x.com/araghchi/status/2122719887659311376?a=rFY0hQGvvAgmHjIdr6I&s=46) the claims "RUBBISH" and accused U.S. media of reviving the propaganda tactics that justified the 2003 U.S. invasion of Iraq. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf similarly [dismissed](https://x.com/mb_ghalibaf/status/2122713966334066728?a=mwlYa3SLeKiWrKnyt0g&s=46) the reports as the "same false flags, same war mongering, new logos."

  * **U.S. Navy says Iran war is straining resources, requiring use of previously expired munitions:** The war with Iran is "stressing our naval resources," Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao [said](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/us-iran-navy-hormuz-war-cao.html) on Tuesday during his Senate confirmation hearing. The Navy has begun using previously expired munitions to stem the shortages, he said. He also said that 17 Navy destroyers were supporting the U.S. blockade of Iranian ships at an estimated cost of $32.5 million a day.

  * **Iran says it downed U.S. drone near Hormuz:** Iran's military claimed on Wednesday that it shot down a U.S. MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz.

  * **AI models repeatedly identify civilians, Iranian school as military targets, study finds:** Advanced AI models from eight companies, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and xAI, repeatedly identified civilians, ambulances, surrendering soldiers, and civilian infrastructure as military targets in simulated scenarios, Bloomberg [reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-17/top-ai-models-regularly-identify-civilians-as-military-targets-in-tests). The models frequently identified as a military target the school in Minab, Iran, where the U.S. military killed at least 156 people, 120 of them children, in a strike earlier this year.

    * In an earlier investigation, Bloomberg [reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/graphics/2026-iran-school-attack/) that the Minab school had been placed on a U.S. military target list after being classified as part of an IRGC naval facility. The targeting process included input from Palantir's Maven AI system.

    * Earlier this year, Drop Site News published an in-depth account of the U.S. attack on Minab, including testimony from first responders, witnesses, and survivors. **Read the full report[here](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/minab-school-massacre-iran-war-children-families).**

# Palestine

  * **Israeli attacks kill three Palestinians across Gaza:** Israeli strikes killed three Palestinians and wounded others on Wednesday in separate attacks on Deir al-Balah, Al-Maghraqa, and Sheikh Ajlin, three neighborhoods southwest of Gaza City.

    * Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed seven Palestinians, including one who succumbed to earlier injuries, and wounded 15 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.

    * Israeli forces shot and killed a six-year-old Palestinian boy, Eyas Al-Namnam, near his displaced family's tent east of Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza, on Tuesday.

    * Eyas had woken up and was doing homework when his mother asked him to go to his aunt's nearby tent. "Three shots were fired at him," his brother, Abdul Karim Al-Namnam, told Drop Site contributor Mohamed Ahmed. "Two bullets struck the ground and one hit him in the chest." **Watch the dispatch from Ahmed[here](https://x.com/dropsitenews/status/2122771849495097427?a=ijoQgjiyBx2IihBFhig&s=46).**

    * The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,710 killed and 176,131 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,658 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 6,000, while 850 bodies have been recovered.

  * **Israeli forces launch first large-scale military operation in central Gaza since "ceasefire":** The Israeli military said on Wednesday that it had launched a "concentrated operation" in three areas of central Gaza near the "yellow line," west of the Israeli military zone established under the October 2025 ceasefire agreement. The military said that the operation was intended to eliminate "threats" to its forces. It closed parts of Salah al-Din Road, a main thoroughfare that runs north-south along the length of the enclave. Israeli military vehicles and bulldozers had begun advancing toward Salah al-Din Road from Al-Maghraqa, in central Gaza, Drop Site contributor Abdel Qader Sabbah reported.

  * **Israel restricts medical evacuations, Gaza Health Ministry says; over 21,000 patients await treatment abroad:** Israel continues to restrict medical evacuations, Gaza's Health Ministry said. Only 22 people, including patients and caregivers, were permitted to leave Gaza on Tuesday, although more than 21,000 people requiring medical care await evacuation. The October 2025 ceasefire provisions permit up to 150 people to leave for treatment every week.

    * In October, the UN planned to stop receiving Palestinians returning from Egypt to Gaza in mid-November, citing security risks and repeated Israeli arrests, a senior Palestinian source involved in negotiations [told](https://x.com/dropsitenews/status/2113285390278742029?a=Jf7pQjdHclx1d59Hxt8&s=46) Drop Site News. The source warned that the decision could disrupt the entire Rafah crossing operation. The ceasefire agreement requires that equal numbers of Palestinians enter and leave Gaza, potentially blocking further medical evacuations.

  * **Israeli forces detain 26 Palestinians across occupied West Bank:**

    * **Hebron:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/18/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B2%D9%84%D8%A7-%D9%85%D8%A3%D9%87%D9%88%D9%84%D8%A7-%D9%88%D8%BA%D8%B1%D9%81%D8%A9-%D8%B2%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%81%D9%8A) a house in Beit Awwa, west of Hebron, on Wednesday, according to WAFA. In Idhna, soldiers demolished an agricultural facility and uprooted olive trees. Across the governorate, soldiers arrested five Palestinians.

    * **Tulkarm:** Israeli forces [arrested](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/18/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%84-14-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D8%A7-%D9%85%D9%86-%D8%B7%D9%88%D9%84%D9%83%D8%B1%D9%85-%D9%88%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%A7) 14 Palestinians, including a woman, and damaged Palestinian property during raids on homes in Tulkarm city and Bal'a.

    * **Jenin:** An Israeli settler [stole](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/18/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%84-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%AB%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%AE%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%AA%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%A1) olive-harvesting equipment from a Palestinian family in Arraba, south of Jenin, before summoning Israeli soldiers to the area. The soldiers subsequently raided the family's homes, assaulted residents, threw stun grenades inside houses, destroyed surveillance cameras, and arrested two family members.

    * **Qalqilya:** Israeli soldiers [arrested](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/18/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%84-%D8%AE%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%A9-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%86%D9%87%D9%85-%D8%B5%D8%AD%D9%81%D9%8A-%D9%85%D9%86) five Palestinians, including Palestine TV cameraman Mohammad Inaya, during raids on homes across the city.

  * **Israel orders land seizure in Tulkarm and Nur Shams refugee camps:** An Israeli military order to seize land in the Tulkarm and Nur Shams refugee camps in the West Bank threatens to prevent thousands of forcibly displaced Palestinians from returning and rebuilding their homes, the Popular Committee for Tulkarm Camp Services [said](https://yaffaps.com/en/page-143332.html) on Tuesday. Israeli forces have maintained a siege of the two camps since January 2025. Soldiers have blocked residents from entering the camps, while demolishing and bulldozing the areas.

  * **Israel extends detention of Gaza hospital director Hussam Abu Safiya another six months without charge:** On Wednesday, an Israeli court [extended](https://x.com/hussamabusafiya/status/2123040943070642647?a=0YqvvmrS-tl6hK-P1xs&s=46) the detention of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, former director of Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza, for another six months. Israeli forces detained him nearly two years ago, on December 27, 2024. Since then, Abu Safiya, 53, has been imprisoned without charge or trial. His lawyers and human-rights groups say that Israeli authorities have beaten him, deprived him of sleep, held him in solitary confinement, and degraded his health.

    * The court rejected his request for release, his lawyer said, ruling that he "poses a threat to the State of Israel." Abu Safiya questioned the renewal of his detention, saying that he was being punished for fulfilling his professional duty as a doctor.

  * **U.S.-backed Board of Peace says Gaza ceasefire risks collapse:** On Tuesday, the U.S.-backed Board of Peace [told](https://apnews.com/article/board-of-peace-us-israel-gaza-hamas-189d58d05fa984cc9573f98ec7d638be) the UN Security Council that the October 2025 Gaza ceasefire could collapse. In a report, the Board of Peace faulted both Israel and Hamas for failing to fully implement the ceasefire agreement. Hamas agreed in July to decommission its "heavy" weaponry and transfer governance to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected the plan, refusing to withdraw its military forces from Gaza until Hamas is dismantled.

    * "Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas' agreement to the roadmap to the test," the report said. Since the so-called ceasefire took effect, Israeli attacks have killed more than 1,600 Palestinians, including at least 330 children and 164 women in Gaza.

    * In a rare rebuke, the Board of Peace blamed Israel for delaying the formation of a civilian police force in Gaza, and for restricting the entry of essential supplies as Palestinians face "another winter in tents and rubble."

  * **Australia sanctions Israeli settler leader Daniella Weiss and construction firm over West Bank settlements:** Australia [announced](https://www.dfat.gov.au/news/news/3-persons-and-4-entities-listed-under-autonomous-sanctions-regulations-2011-human-rights-0) sanctions on Wednesday against three individuals and four organizations involved in illegal settlement expansion and human rights abuses against Palestinians in the West Bank. Those sanctioned include the settler leader Daniella Weiss; Weiss's Nachala settler movement; and Eyal Hari Yehuda, a construction company that has aided settlement expansion. It is the first time Australia has sanctioned a company involved in settlement construction. Palestinian advocacy groups and the Greens political party called for broader sanctions, including against the Israeli government and settlement exports.

  * **Hind Rajab Foundation seeks U.S. prosecution of former Israeli defense minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and genocide:** The Hind Rajab Foundation filed a request with the U.S. Justice Department on Tuesday seeking the prosecution of former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes in Gaza and Lebanon, and genocide in Gaza. He is scheduled to appear at an annual summit hosted by MirYam Institute, a pro-Israel organization, in New York City on Wednesday. The International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for Gallant in November 2024 on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity.

# Yemen

  * **Saudi airstrikes kill 15 at factory in Hodeidah, Yemen:** Saudi airstrikes on a factory in Hodeidah, Yemen, killed at least 15 people and wounded 13 others, including factory workers and rescue personnel, according to the Sana'a-based Health Ministry. The ministry said that Saudi jets struck the factory a second time after aid workers and journalists arrived on the scene, seriously wounding four members of a Yemen TV crew. [Footage](https://x.com/dropsitenews/status/2122936271509049694?a=2amn4oEl5xYV9oyP-Ww&s=46) released by Al-Masirah TV showed thick black smoke and flames engulfing the factory following the reported strikes.

  * **Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed 60 Ansarallah targets across Yemen, intercepted missile near Riyadh:** The Saudi-led coalition [said](https://x.com/cjfcspox/status/2122852774375198750?a=cEj2qu_QBebMqzEP8j8&s=46) that it carried out strikes against 60 Ansarallah military targets across the Yemeni governorates of Sana'a, Hodeidah, Amran, and Saada on Wednesday. Coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Malki said that the strikes destroyed tunnels and underground facilities that Ansarallah used to store and produce ballistic missiles.

    * Saudi coalition forces also intercepted and destroyed a missile launched by Ansarallah toward the Riyadh area in Saudi Arabia, Al-Malki said.

# U.S. News

  * **Hakeem Jeffries wins speaker nomination, commits to aggressive agenda on immigration, healthcare ahead of vote:** On Wednesday, Rep. **Hakeem Jeffries**(D-N.Y.) won the nomination for Speaker of the House, overcoming objections from some left-wing Democrats. Much of the opposition came from newly elected Democrats who are aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America. His critics within the party objected to his strong support for Israel, and his opposition to Medicare for All.

    * On Tuesday, Jeffries announced his support for a broadly progressive Democratic agenda. "We're going to move the Dream and Promise Act" in the next Congressional session, he [said](https://www.washingtonsun.com/immigration/jeffries-american-dream-and-promise-act-immigration-congress). The American Dream and Promise Act, introduced by Rep. **Sylvia Garcia** (D-Texas), would grant legal permanent residency to undocumented immigrants who arrived in the U.S. as children, and to people shielded from deportation through Temporary Protected Status. Her discharge petition, which would avoid GOP obstruction, has 217 signatures, just one short of forcing a vote. A Democratic Congress could pass the legislation, but its codification would require President Trump's signature. Following the midterms, Trump said that he might "work a deal" to protect some people who have lived in the U.S. for 10-plus years and who do not have a criminal record.

    * Also on Tuesday, Jeffries [called](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/jeffries-endorses-lowering-medicare-age-adding-benefits-universal-cove-rcna609843) for an aggressive Democratic health care agenda, including lowering the Medicare eligibility age and adding dental, vision, and hearing benefits to the plan. "And we should cover all the kids in the United States of America," he said. His remarks go well beyond earlier promises, in September, to undo Trump's Medicaid cuts and restore expired Affordable Care Act tax credits. Sen. **Bernie Sanders** (I-Vt.) said that Jeffries appears to be "essentially supporting the first year" of Sanders' proposed Medicare for All plan, which would begin by lowering the eligibility age to 55.

  * **NSA reports outage of classified comms system:** An internal National Security Agency communications system was [down](https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/11/17/communications-system-top-secret-national-security-agency-goes-down/) on Tuesday. The outage affected NSA Net, a system for classified communications. The cause is not known, but a former Pentagon official told the Washington Post that the outage delayed employees' work at Fort Meade, in Maryland, and elsewhere. The NSA said that the agency "experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance," adding that "mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational." The outage does not appear to have affected core intelligence-gathering systems.

  * **DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin defends use of government plane to attend college football game: Markwayne Mullin** , secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, [defended](https://apnews.com/article/markwayne-mullin-nationwide-ground-stop-lsu-1155f7fe532f55b272d3b9fefcd68d2b) his flight on a government plane to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, for a college football game between Louisiana State University and the University of Texas on Saturday. He took the flight shortly after the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a national ground stoppage. Mullin said that he took the flight after airspace was "completely open for 21 hours." He added that he is required to travel by government plane, and that he personally paid for the trip.

  * **Kalshi halts bets predicting Trump statements:** Kalshi is halting all bets on President Donald Trump's predicted statements, the Wall Street Journal [reported](https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/kalshi-to-halt-bets-that-are-based-on-trumps-remarks-71bbc94b). The decision comes after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission ordered Kalshi to temporarily stop such bets due to concerns about bet manipulation. Last month, Kalshi's regulatory chief, **Sudhir Jain** , defended these types of bets as having "true hedging utility." Kalshi has not halted betting on the statements of other Trump administration officials. Earlier this year, **Gabriel Perez** , Trump's former teleprompter operator, was penalized for using insider information to place bets on the president's speeches.

  * **Politico: Hegseth 's personal attorney represents son of Libyan warlord: **War Secretary **Pete Hegseth** 's personal attorney **Tim Parlatore** has [represented](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/17/tim-parlatore-libya-warlord-hegseth-01168919) **Saddam Haftar** , who is chief of staff of the Libyan National Army and the son of the Libyan warlord **Khalifa Haftar** , since April, Politico reported. The father and son have been accused of extrajudicial killings and torture in a lawsuit filed by **Mohammed Anbees** , a Libyan man living in the U.S. The attorney representing the Haftars in the case is Parlatore himself.

  * **Pentagon fails annual audit for ninth consecutive year:** The Pentagon [failed](https://thehill.com/policy/defense/6224597-pentagon-fails-ninth-audit/) its annual audit for the ninth consecutive year. The audit found that many of its financial-management systems are either outdated or otherwise inadequate. The audit assessed nearly $5 trillion of its assets and involved about 1,500 auditors. War Secretary **Hegseth** had set a goal of a clean audit by 2028. He has said that the department is using tools from Palantir and **Elon Musk** 's xAI to "automate financial reconciliations and documentation."

  * **Federal appeals court stops Pentagon 's attempt to expel 27 transgender troops from military: **A D.C. Circuit panel voted 2-1 on Tuesday to [prevent](https://apnews.com/article/transgender-military-ban-trump-dc-circuit-dcdb4c91f17e59c7c2dc5fb725d3b7e9) the War Department from expelling 27 transgender troops from the military. The decision will allow transgender troops to remain in their posts, but it does not grant the entree of new transgender recruits. The same court panel ruled in June that the Trump administration's ban on transgender troops was unlawful. The administration has petitioned the Supreme Court to take up the case.

  * **Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years in prison for attempt to assassinate U.S. politician; he says Iran backed the plot:** On Monday, a Pakistani businessman, **Asif Merchant** , was [sentenced](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/justice-department/pakistani-man-asif-merchant-27-years-prison-assassination-plot-trump-rcna609922) to 27 years in prison after he was convicted of trying to kill a U.S. politician in 2024. Possible targets included Donald Trump, **Joe Biden** , and **Nikki Haley** , according to trial testimony. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard urged Merchant to kill one of the targets, he said, adding that the IRGC assigned a handler to him. Iran has denied trying to kill U.S. officials. Merchant was caught after paying $5,000 in cash to undercover FBI agents posing as hit men. He was arrested in Texas in July 2024.

  * **Mary Peltola wins Senate race in Alaska, bringing Dem majority to 56 seats:** Democrat**Mary Peltola** [defeated](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/17/politics/mary-peltola-wins-alaska-senate) Republican Sen. **Dan Sullivan** in Alaska's Senate race, becoming Alaska's first Native American senator and winning in a state that Trump won by 13 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. Her win brings the Democratic Senate majority to 56 seats. The Peltola-Sullivan race was controversial: The Justice Department accused Peltola's camp of getting a spoiler candidate onto the ballot, whose name is also **Dan Sullivan**. The DOJ opened a formal investigation of the incident, which has stalled in the courts. But Republican governor-elect **Mike Dunleavy** has said that Alaska could withhold Peltola's election certification while the investigation continues.

  * **NYT: IRS pursuing criminal investigations of left-wing groups:** The Internal Revenue Service has [opened](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/17/us/politics/irs-criminal-investigations.html) at least four criminal investigations into left-wing groups, the New York Times reported, citing an internal memo. The memo shows that a dozen IRS officials are detailed to a federal task force under President Trump's 2025 order to investigate antifascists and groups espousing "extremism on migration, race and gender." The task force referred at least four tax-exempt groups to civil auditors. The IRS officials were assigned to nine grand juries, and used facial recognition and tattoo-analysis databases to investigate protesters arrested at Delaney Hall, an immigrant detention center in Newark, New Jersey.

  * **White House abandons FDA nominee:** The White House [rescinded](https://www.washingtonpost.com/health/2026/11/17/white-house-pulls-fda-nominee-amid-bipartisan-pushback/) its nomination of **Heidi Overton** to lead the Food and Drug Administration ahead of a Senate vote scheduled for Wednesday. The move comes after pushback from Democratic and Republican senators. **Bill Cassidy** , chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions committee, said on Sunday that he had "questions" about her nomination. Overton, deputy director of the White House Domestic Policy Council, has faced numerous criticisms, including over an executive order to alter the childhood vaccine schedule and to break up the measles vaccine. The FDA has operated without a permanent commissioner since **Marty Makary** resigned from the post in May.

  * **DOJ misconduct complaints rise 54% under second Trump administration:** Professional misconduct complaints against DOJ personnel [rose](https://www.washingtonsun.com/agencies/complaints-doj-officials) 54% under Trump's second term, relative to those filed during the Biden administration. The Office of Professional Responsibility received 2,081 complaints last fiscal year, up from 1,346 in 2024. The report also noted a net decline of 10,345 department employees between January 2025 and May 2026.

  * **Massachusetts town passes BDS measure:** The City Council of Somerville, Massachusetts, [voted](https://www.newarab.com/news/us-city-somerville-approves-israel-divestment-measure) 10-1 on Tuesday to restrict city contracts and investments in companies linked to abuses in Palestine. Somerville is the fifth city in Massachusetts, and the 30th in the U.S., to adopt a measure in line with the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement, and the first to name Israel and Palestine explicitly in its operative language. The ordinance uses two databases maintained by the United Nations and the American Friends Service Committee to identify companies deemed complicit in abuses.

  * **U.S. soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of spying for Russia is transferred to U.S. military custody:** A senior U.S. soldier [assigned](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/17/uk-hands-nato-assigned-us-soldier-accused-of-russia-spying-to-us-military) to NATO who was arrested in the UK last week on suspicion of spying for Russia was transferred to U.S. military custody, the UK's Counter Terrorism Policing announced Tuesday.   * **Mexico 's Sheinbaum tells China's Xi she wants deeper economic cooperation: **Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum [said](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/mexico-keen-strengthen-cooperation-with-china-president-says-2026-11-17/) in a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday that Mexico is interested in strengthening cooperation with China in technology, agriculture, water resources, health, and tourism. The two leaders met in Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Chinese state media reported that Xi urged the two countries to "treat each other with sincerity, deepen political mutual trust," promote friendly cooperation and strengthen strategic alignment.

  * **Peru 's Fujimori seeks China's help on El Niño, says Beijing pledged $22.5 million in aid:** Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori [appealed](https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/peru-appeals-chinese-goodwill-help-110931739.html) for China's "goodwill" and support at a Tuesday meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, ahead of the APEC summit, and said Beijing pledged $22.5 million to help Peru cope with El Niño. Scientists say warmer ocean temperatures tied to El Niño are disrupting marine ecosystems off Peru's coast, threatening the fishing industry, and putting more than 1 million people in climate-vulnerable regions at risk.

  * **Clashes between police and garment workers in Bangladesh escalate:** Bangladeshi police [fired](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/11/1/bangladesh-workers-clash-with-police-in-protests-over-low-pay) tear gas and stun grenades at thousands of garment workers protesting a postponed wage board meeting on Tuesday. The protesters reportedly hurled bricks, torched vehicles, and blocked the main highway between Dhaka and Mymensingh after a key wage board meeting was postponed. About 500 of the country's 4,500 garment factories are shut, AFP reported, in an industry that earns $38 billion a year and employs more than four million people. Bangladesh is the world's second-biggest garment exporter.

  * **Over 146,000 take to French streets as public-sector workers demand pay raises amid rising cost of living:** France's Interior Ministry [said](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/14/more-than-100000-rally-across-france-in-new-yellow-vest-protests) 146,000 people joined Tuesday's protests by public sector workers, estimating 28,000 in Paris alone, while the General Confederation of Labor put the nationwide turnout at just over 500,000. School pupils and university students struck in solidarity with the public sector workers, the third such strike since September. Unions say public servants have lost 16 percent of their purchasing power since 2017 and want the pay scale point used to calculate basic salary unfrozen, but the government has ruled out a general pay rise for a fourth consecutive year in its draft budget.

  * **Mozambique opposition leader goes on trial:** Mozambique's main opposition leader, Venancio Mondlane, went on [trial](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/mozambiques-main-opposition-leader-goes-trial-over-post-election-unrest-2026-11-17/) Tuesday at the Supreme Court in Maputo on charges of inciting terrorism and civil disobedience over the unrest that followed the country's 2024 vote. Mondlane denies all charges and calls the proceedings politically motivated. A civil society monitoring group says more than 300 people were killed in the protests, the largest ever against the ruling Frelimo party, which has governed since independence in 1975. The opposition says President Daniel Chapo and Frelimo won through vote-rigging, and Western observers said the vote was not free and fair.

  * **Trump announces critical-minerals agreements with Quad partners India, Australia and Japan at Manila meeting:** President Trump [said](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/17/trump-announces-critical-minerals-agreements-at-quad-meeting-in-manila) leaders of the Quad, which also includes Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, reached agreements to secure supply chains for critical minerals and prevent "coercion by any single foreign supplier." Trump did not single out China, which dominates the global market for rare-earth elements, but said he plans to "catch" China's production of rare earths within 10 months. The agreement also notes concerns about "economic coercion," given China's predominance in the market. China has effectively cut off key critical-mineral exports to Japan for nearly a year.
